Subject: Re: Question re: smtpd_tls_security_level

Jorey Bump, on 2/11/2008 11:24 AM, said the following:
> Charles Marcus wrote, at 02/11/2008 10:53 AM:
>> The man page for this setting states:
>>
>> "Note 2: The parameter setting "smtpd_tls_security_level = encrypt" 
>> implies "smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes"."
>>
>> I just want to confirm that if I set this to encrypt, then I do NOT 
>> need to set "smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes"...?
>>
>> Currently I have both, but if I don't need the auth_only, no sense in 
>> setting it.

> Since the default is smtpd_tls_auth_only = no, you should explicitly set 
> it to "yes" to prevent any changes to smtpd_tls_security_level from 
> exposing user passwords.

Ok... I'm not arguing, just wanting clarification, because that is not 
how I read what the man page says... if you are correct, then in my 
opinion the word 'implies' on the man page should be changed to 'requires'.

Could someone else who knows for a fact the answer to this please chime in?

Thanks,

-- 

Best regards,

Charles
